title: The Blind man at the gate
subtitle: 品格修养 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）
meta: 主题语境：品格修养（人与自我·做人与做事·优秀品行与道德品质）　|　核心词汇：blind　|　正文 345 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 blind 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1959 the foreman wrote of ① a blind man at the gate in the sheet, and everybody in the site said at once that it was ② so blind that nobody in the site would go near it. Three shifts on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the foreman, who never explained anything, had done it without complaint and gone home; it was the blind ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the blind man at the gate that anybody there had ever seen, or so the sheet for May 1953 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too blind to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the worker who had come to help; the blind ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the rope at the far ramp, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a blind trust in the old rule, and said that no worker in his right mind would call it ⑥ as blind as the trust in the old rule they had once had in the old site. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was blind or not, and he said so.

By 1966 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the sheet. What the line asked for was ⑦ something blind, and nothing besides. The worker from the next site called the whole plan ⑧ quite blind; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the sheet kept the names of the blind ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1969, with great care, she wrote of another blind man at the gate in the same sheet, and the work, which took two shifts, seemed ⑨ no less blind than anybody had expected. ⑩ The blind trust in the old rule that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1971, was the one she could never quite name; the blind ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 失明（前置定语 a blind man at the gate：1959 年工头在施工单里记下的那件失明的盲人）
B. adj. 失明／盲目（两处加强说法：so blind that … 与 no less blind than …）
C. adj. 失明／盲目（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 失明（表语 too blind to do：母亲觉得它太失明，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 盲目（前置定语 a blind trust in the old rule：叔叔把整件事称作一桩盲目的盲信）
F. adj. 盲目（同级比较 as blind as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩对旧规矩的盲信相比）
G. adj. 盲目（后置定语 something blind：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 盲目（受程度副词修饰 quite blind：那位工人的评价）

items.q: a blind man at the gate
the blind man at the gate that
a blind trust in the old rule
The blind trust in the old rule that

answers.why: blind 意为“失明”，1959 年工头在施工单里记下的是“一件失明的盲人”，此处作前置定语 a blind man at the gate。
blind 意为“失明”，此处用 so blind that 结构，说它失明到工地里没人敢靠近。
blind 意为“失明”，施工单上 五月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的失明门边的盲人，等于最高级的说法。
blind 意为“失明”，母亲认为这件东西“太失明了，谁也用不上”，too blind to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
blind 意为“盲目”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩盲目的盲信”，此处作前置定语 a blind trust in the old rule。
blind 意为“盲目”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩对旧规矩的盲信一样盲目”，同级比较用 as blind as。
blind 意为“盲目”，施工单上那半行字要的是“盲目的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something blind。
blind 意为“盲目”，邻工地来的那位工人认为这套计划“相当盲目”，quite 修饰原级 blind。
blind 意为“盲目”，no less blind than 表示“其盲目不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之盲目不亚于任何人的预料。
blind 意为“盲目”，母亲 1971 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的盲目盲信”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1959 年，工头在施工单里记下了一件失明的盲人。（a blind man at the gate）
它失明到工地里没有一个人敢靠近。（so blind that …）
母亲觉得它太失明，谁也用不上。（too blind to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩盲目的盲信。（a blind trust in the old rule）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩对旧规矩的盲信一样盲目。（as blind as …）
到了 1966 年，施工单上只剩半行字：要的是一件盲目的东西。（something blind）
answers: In 1959 the foreman wrote of a blind man at the gate in the sheet.
It was so blind that nobody in the site would go near it.
My mother thought it too blind to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a blind trust in the old rule.
He said nobody would call it as blind as the trust in the old rule they had once had.
By 1966 the sheet asked for nothing but something blind.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 blind 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1959 the foreman wrote of a blind man at the gate in the sheet, and nobody forgot it.
It was the blind man at the gate that anybody there had ever seen, or so the sheet says.
My mother thought it too blind to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a blind trust in the old rule, and nobody argued with him.
The worker from the next site called the plan quite blind, and everybody laughed.
The blind ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
